3.2a — Projectiles: Instantiate, Fire, Destroy

Today the turret actually shoots. A bullet is born, flies, dies — a whole life in a few frames, built from the prefab factory you learned in 2.4a plus one new idea: pointing a vector at a target.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the fire path in TurretController.cs:

private void AttackPlayer()
{
    Quaternion rotation = Quaternion.LookRotation(Vector3.forward, playerController.transform.position - projectileSpawnPoint.position);

    GameObject proj = Instantiate(projectilePrefab, projectileSpawnPoint.position, rotation);
    proj.GetComponent<Projectile>().Initialize(playerController.transform.position);
}

And the flight half of Projectile.cs:

public void Initialize(Vector3 targetPos)
{
    Vector3 direction = (targetPos - transform.position).normalized;
    float angle = Mathf.Atan2(direction.y, direction.x) * Mathf.Rad2Deg;
    transform.rotation = Quaternion.AngleAxis(angle, Vector3.forward);
}

private void Update()
{
    transform.Translate(Vector3.right * speed * Time.deltaTime);
}

Predict the flight: the projectile does NOT steer toward you after you dodge. It aims at where you were when it fired and flies straight forever (or 5 seconds — find the line that kills it). Where is the "forever" stopped, and what would the game look like without it?

Socratic

Why does Initialize take the target position instead of steering toward the player every frame? What would the projectile be if it did chase you — and which enemy in this game already behaves that way?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — the plumbing. Select the Turret instance. The Inspector shows two empty slots the code needs: Projectile Prefab and Projectile Spawn Point. Drag the Turret_Projectile prefab into the first. For the second, the turret prefab has a child Transform near its muzzle — drag that into the slot. The script now knows what to stamp and where from. This wiring — code declares slots, the Inspector fills them — is how every designer-configurable behavior in Unity works.

Step 2 — the aim, unpacked. Read Initialize again in three moves: (1) target - spawn is the vector that points at you; (2) .normalized keeps the direction but throws away the length — remember the diagonal in 1.5a? (3) Atan2 turns the direction into an angle, and the rotation points the projectile's "right" at you. Then Update flies it along its own right, forever-ish. The math is one old friend (vectors) plus one new one (rotation).

Step 3 — walk the life cycle. Press Play and step in range. One projectile: Instantiate (born at the spawn point) → Initialize (aims) → Update (flies) → then it dies twice over: hit the player and OnTriggerEnter2D in Projectile.cs destroys it (and ChangeHealth(-damage) — the hurt from 2.2a, reused), or miss and Destroy(gameObject, lifetime) kills it after 5 seconds. Every bullet needs a death; the turret's is pre-installed on both paths.

Bug Hunt: The misfire catalog

  1. Empty the Projectile Prefab slot and press Play. What is the error, and which line caused it?
  2. Swap the spawn point to a child at the turret's FEET. What visually changes and what does that say about who chose the muzzle?
  3. In Projectile.Update change Vector3.right to Vector3.up. Where do bullets go now — and what is "right" relative to, anyway?
  4. Set lifetime to 999. Why do dodge-strafing duels suddenly lag? Where do old bullets actually go?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: The bullet designer

  1. Open the Turret_Projectile prefab and tune its speed and damage like a designer. What speed makes dodging feel possible rather than lucky?
  2. Make the projectile bigger and slower — a "cannonball" variant. What changed about the GAME feel, with zero lines of code?
  3. Hard: a bullet that splits into three after 0.5 seconds. Which script would instantiate — and what would Initialize take as target?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Wire prefab + spawn point slots in the Inspector and say why that pattern exists
  • Trace the aim: direction → normalize → Atan2 → rotation → translate along right
  • Explain both of the projectile's deaths (hit + lifetime) and why both are needed
  • Tune a projectile variant with code untouched
